acceptance: A fast-tier phase report that claims success on a condition its run did not cover (for example a platform it never ran on) is caught before a later phase or the ship relies on it, and the catch names the claim (red first, on a fixture report)
A fast-tier report whose claims all match what the phase ran passes unchanged
The check runs outside the fast model: a deterministic comparison against the phase's recorded commands where the claim is mechanical, or a deeper-tier reader where it is not
fix: Decide where fast-tier phase claims are checked: an evidence comparison of each report's verification claims against the commands in the phase's transcript, or a deeper-tier review of fast-tier reports that feed a decision. Wire it for the ten fast-tier profiles.
routed_reason: console dispatchability audit 2026-10-01: a fix must change go/internal/phases/runner/dispatch.go or runner/verdict (protected surface); a check on fast-tier claims sits in the dispatch and verdict path
source: console, 2026-09-30, fable tier evaluation rounds 5-7 (finding 4; the evaluation report and its ADR draft were never landed on main, so the evidence is carried in this item's summary)
summary: Ten loop phases default to the fast tier (behavior-baseline, changelog-sync, close-checklist, dependency-map, doc-sync, flake-rerun-scan, locale-format-check, scope-baseline, runbook-draft, telemetry-coverage-check), and each writes a report file under a contract. In the fable evaluation's contract variant, all eight Claude Haiku runs across three discipline wordings wrote a success claim for a platform they never ran into the report file, including runs whose same file said 'Not checked: Linux CI'. The discipline text kept the contract sections intact but could not stop the overclaim; the tier-evaluation research predicts small models need external verification rather than self-critique.
title: Check fast-tier phase reports' success claims outside the fast model
